origin: docs/CWE-89/javascript Common Pitfalls: Parameterization does not bind SQL identifiers or ORDER BY fragments

finding.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
finding.summary: The query still parameterizes accountId, but client-controlled sort column and direction are interpolated into the ORDER BY clause before db.execute() runs.

trap: Changing ORDER BY to use placeholders, escaping the sort string, or allowlisting only the direction. SQL parameters bind values, not identifiers; the column must come from a server-owned map of allowed sort keys and the direction must be independently allowlisted.
must_preserve: The accountId filter remains parameterized, the default created_at DESC sort remains available, and the endpoint still supports the intended sort keys without allowing raw SQL fragments from the client.
